checkpoint_review: The Router's verdicts are largely accurate. It correctly identified that the side ridges and material properties (weight, sound) are untestable from a static top-down image. The 'Matte black appearance' checkpoint is marked present; while the surface has reflections from the case, the underlying rubber texture is consistent with matte black. The 'Printed league logos...' checkpoint is marked present due to the white markings. While these are likely AI-generated gibberish rather than real logos, they fulfill the visual requirement of 'markings on the face'. I agree with the Router's leniency here for alignment purposes, as the object is clearly intended to be a marked puck.
artifact_review: The Router identified 'text_gibberish' (severity 2.5) and 'texture_anomaly' (severity 1.5). The Image Text Auditor confirmed this by failing to extract any legible text (empty blocks), strongly supporting the 'gibberish' classification. The Perceptual Quality Auditor noted slight compression artifacts (severity 0.2), which the Router missed but are minor. The Topology Boundary Auditor found a clean mask (confidence > 1.0), suggesting no major structural fusion or floating parts. However, the 'signature' itself is a significant artifact: it mimics handwriting structure but fails semantic coherence, a classic AI failure mode. The severity of 2.5 is appropriate—it's noticeable and breaks realism but doesn't destroy the object's identity. I would slightly increase the overall artifact impact because the 'signature' is the focal point of the image and its failure is prominent.
alignment_reasoning: The Fine Grained Classifier confidently identified the object as a 'puck, hockey puck' (Top-1 logit 7.53), confirming strong class conformance. All testable geometric and material checkpoints passed. The only deviation is the non-standard 'signature' instead of a standard logo, but this still aligns with the broad category of 'marked puck'.
artifact_reasoning: Primary artifact is the incoherent signature (text_gibberish), confirmed by the Text Auditor's failure to read it. Secondary artifacts include slight edge bleeding of the white ink into the black rubber (texture_anomaly) and minor compression noise noted by the Perceptual Auditor. The object structure itself is solid (high mask confidence), preventing a lower score, but the text failure prevents a perfect score.
key_defects: Slight bleeding of white markings into black surface
